data.description:
npm run pr-gate is red on main right now, and will stay red on every branch until this is fixed. 22 tests fail. None of them are about the change under test.

The cause is a frozen clock meeting a real one. tests/integration/api/participants-editable.MRQ-139.test.ts:59 pins the fixture's notion of now:

  const now = Date.UTC(2026, 7, 12, 12, 0, 0);

and mints the organizer's session with expires_at = now + 86_400_000 — 2026-08-13T12:00:00Z. But resolveSession (src/lib/auth/auth-sessions.ts:45-57) validates with 'expires_at > ?' bound to the REAL Date.now(). So the fixture session was born already counting down against wall-clock time, and it died at 12:00 UTC today. Every request in the file now answers 401. tests/integration/api/people.MRQ-131.test.ts:92 has the same shape and fails the same way.

That is the whole of it: 8 failures in MRQ-139 plus 14 in MRQ-131 equals the 22. The product is not broken, and neither is the change that happened to be on main when it fired.

Two things make this worth a high priority rather than a shrug:

1. It is not self-limiting. It went red at 12:00 UTC 2026-08-13 and it does not come back. Every agent who runs the gate from now on sees a red suite caused by nothing they did.
2. It teaches the fleet to ignore a red gate, which is the expensive failure. A gate that is red for reasons unrelated to the diff is worse than no gate — it converts the one signal that should stop a merge into noise. This project already merged PR #136 over a REQUEST CHANGES and merged PR #169 on an admittedly stale gate; a permanently-red suite makes that the norm rather than the exception.

Scope. Sixteen test files insert into auth_sessions with an expiry offset. Most compute now from Date.now(), so their sessions are always valid and they are fine. Only the ones that pin a literal date are bombs:

  - participants-editable.MRQ-139.test.ts — Date.UTC(2026,7,12,12,0,0) + 24h — FIRING since 2026-08-13T12:00Z
  - people.MRQ-131.test.ts — same shape — FIRING
  - submission-record-board.AC-118-120-238-240-243-251.test.ts — Date.UTC(2026,9,20,15,30) + 24h — fires 2026-10-21, currently green and will look fine right up until it is not

Acceptance criteria:
1. The gate is green on main with no other change.
2. Fixture sessions cannot expire against the wall clock. Either mint expires_at from Date.now() rather than the fixture's frozen now, or give resolveSession's now a test-injectable value the fixture controls — the first is smaller, the second is more honest about the coupling. Pick one and apply it to all three files, not just the two that are currently red.
3. A check that would have caught this before a date boundary rather than after: no test may insert an auth_sessions row whose expires_at is computed from a literal date. A grep-level check in scripts/checks is enough; it does not need to be clever.
4. Sweep for the same frozen-clock-vs-real-clock shape in other expiry-checked tables — magic_links.expires_at and forms.closes_at are the obvious neighbours.

Files: tests/integration/api/participants-editable.MRQ-139.test.ts (:59, :63-65), tests/integration/api/people.MRQ-131.test.ts (:92), tests/integration/api/submission-record-board.AC-118-120-238-240-243-251.test.ts, src/lib/auth/auth-sessions.ts (:45-57, the real-clock read).

Provenance: found while gating 07dd8870 before a deploy. I first mis-attributed it to PR #157, which was the newest commit; checking out e29d4bd8 — which had gated clean 30 minutes earlier — reproduced the identical 8 failures, which is what ruled the diff out and the clock in.
data.title: A test fixture mints auth sessions against a frozen clock, so the gate goes red on a date nobody chose

provenance.reason: Discovered gating main 07dd8870 for deploy; the gate is now permanently red for every agent on every branch

data.body:
Status update and a re-scope — the symptom is fixed, the cause is not.

PR #171 merged (a04f80b1) and fixed the four armed fixtures: people.MRQ-131, participants-editable.MRQ-139, agent-evaluator.MRQ-134, evaluation-override.MRQ-149. That list is better than the one in this ticket's description — it caught MRQ-134 and MRQ-149, which I missed.

Two corrections to my own description, so nobody works from the wrong map:

1. AC 3 named tests/integration/api/submission-record-board.AC-118-120-238-240-243-251.test.ts as a third bomb firing 2026-10-21. THAT IS WRONG. It uses 'const now = Date.now()' at line 42 and is safe. The Date.UTC(2026, 9, 20, 15, 30) I flagged is an agenda item's starts_at payload at line 143, not a session clock. My grep took the first Date.UTC in the file and I did not check what it fed.
2. AC 4 asked for a new grep-level guard. One already exists: scripts/checks/check-clocks.mjs, wired into pr-gate.mjs:37, written after a 2026-08-12 incident whose docstring describes THIS EXACT failure mode — 'a fixture that says const NOW = Date.UTC(...) and then writes expires_at: NOW + 86_400_000'.

Which leaves the finding that actually matters. I checked out 17242b06 — the commit immediately before #171, with all four files armed and the suite red — and ran the checker:

  [check:clocks] no calendar-pinned deadlines, no burst-spent limits
  status: pass, findings: []

The guard built to prevent this exact recurrence did not see it. It passed clean while four files were armed and two had already detonated. So the gate never had a chance to stop this, and file five will arm itself the same way.

REMAINING SCOPE for this ticket — the cause, not the symptom:

1. Determine why check:clocks missed all four. Read the detector, then prove the gap by running it against 17242b06 as above and showing what it does not match.
2. Close the gap so the four pre-#171 files WOULD have been caught. The test for the fix is exactly that: the repaired checker must fail against 17242b06 and pass against current main. A checker that only passes today proves nothing — it is the same bug with a later fuse.
3. AC 5 stands and is untouched by #171: sweep magic_links.expires_at and forms.closes_at for the same frozen-clock-versus-real-clock shape. Report what you find even if you change nothing.

AC 1 and AC 2 are satisfied by #171. Do not redo them.

PR #178 open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/178

Re-scoped per the operator's mid-run correction. #171 disarmed the four fixtures (AC 1-2 done, not redone here); AC 3's third file was a misdiagnosis — submission-record-board line 42 is `Date.now()`, and the `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 20, 15, 30)` at line 143 is an agenda `starts_at` request payload, never a persisted deadline. AC 4's guard already existed. So the work was the real finding underneath: check:clocks was blind to the exact failure its own docstring describes.

**Root cause.** The rule required a time-compared column and a fixture-anchor offset on the SAME LINE. A prepared statement is not a line — the column lives in the SQL string and the offset over in `.bind(...)`, which is how every INSERT in this repo is written. Reproduced at 17242b06 with all four armed: "no calendar-pinned deadlines", status pass, findings [].

**Fix.** The rule reads prepared statements, quote-aware so SQL parens don't end one early. Two rules follow: an `auth_sessions` row may not carry a calendar date at all, and `createSession` may not be handed a pinned clock (same defect, no INSERT for a statement rule to read). Rules extracted to `clock-policy.mjs` as a pure function over source, following the check-repo/repo-policy precedent.

**Both directions demonstrated.** Repaired checker FAILS at 17242b06 (31 findings, all four fixtures among them) and PASSES on this branch. The new regression suite fails 6 of 8 against the pre-fix rule; the 2 that pass are negative controls a blind checker satisfies for free and prove nothing on their own.

**Found beyond #171, all fixed:**
- delivery-health.MRQ-74 filed a CFP closing 2026-08-15 against a route reading `Date.now()` — two days from firing, in the same file that already documents this exact defect for its sent_today row.
- sessionize-import minted a session dated 2026-08-11, expired since the 12th (green only because the suite authenticates via magic link and never uses that row).
- mail.test.ts passed its 2026-08-10 anchor to `createSession` five times.

Eleven deliberate hits now carry their own stated reason rather than a blanket exemption.

**AC 5 sweep.** magic_links is clean — no test inserts one, every `mintMagicLink` rides `Date.now()`. forms.closes_at yielded the delivery-health defect plus three injected-clock windows, verified and marked. evaluation_rounds.opens_at/closes_at is stored and echoed, never enforced against a clock. Noted but not fixed: submissions-list.test.ts:96 writes a literal `4102444800000` — a literal date with a 74-year fuse, which no rule catches and none should.

**Gate.** `npm run pr-gate` PASS. 1001/1001 tests, 148/148 files. Suite 74s against a 45s objective under load average 65 with 24 sibling vitest/workerd processes; my own baseline of the same suite earlier in the session was 51s. Machine load, recorded rather than rounded off.

Awaiting review before merge.

provenance.reason: scope settled after the operator's mid-run re-scope

data.body: Validation evidence, both directions. Repaired checker at 17242b06 (four fixtures armed): exit 1, 31 findings, all four among them. Same checker on this branch: exit 0, no findings. Original checker at 17242b06 for contrast: exit 0, findings []. Regression suite tests/node/check-clocks.test.mjs: 8/8 pass here, 6/8 fail against the pre-fix rule wrapped in the same signature — the 2 that pass are negative controls and prove nothing alone. npm run pr-gate PASS end to end: 1001/1001 tests, 148/148 files, every check green.

Post-merge validation, run against merged main (cddfc27e), not against the branch. check:clocks: pass, no findings. tests/node/check-clocks.test.mjs: 8/8. The merged guard replayed against 17242b06 with all four fixtures armed: exit 1, 31 findings, all four caught (people.MRQ-131, participants-editable.MRQ-139, agent-evaluator.MRQ-134, evaluation-override.MRQ-149). Both directions hold on main, which is the contract this ticket asked for. CI fast-gate SUCCESS on the rebased head before merge.
